Subject: Acme onramp & ops handoff proposal

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — great to hear more about Acme's latency and cost targets for inference at peak. Per our discussion, attached is a concise commercial offer and an ops handoff outline that maps the first 90 days of the pilot and the production cutover. Highlights:

- 3-month pilot (1 GPU cluster, up to 3M tokens/day) with waived first-month runtime charges if mutually successful
- Matched onboarding credit to offset migration carry cost (details in the attached PDF)
- Standard SLA with optional 24/7 incident support for an additional fee; we can discuss exception terms if you need stricter SLAs

Please review the offer and let me know any gaps you want us to cover. If procurement prefers a single PO + SOW, we can produce both.

Attachment: Redwood-Acme-Commercial-Offer.pdf (summary + line items)

Next step: are you available early next week for a short legal/commercial sync with your procurement and our contracts lead?

Cheers,
Jordan

From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 11:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme onramp & ops handoff proposal

Jordan —

Thanks for sending. A couple of procurement questions and asks from our side before we route to legal:

1) Pricing: Acme has received a competing offer with a temporary usage credit that equates to ~30% effective discount in year one. Can Redwood match that effective economics for migration?
2) Data residency & audit logs: we need confirmation that audit logs for inference requests are retained for 13 months and accessible via API.
3) SLA exceptions: the competitor is offering a 99.9% latency SLO for our region; is there a commercial allowance for performance credits if we do not meet the SLO?

Also include the SOW template and the contact for your contracts lead in the loop. Our timeline: procurement decision targeted by 2027-07-08.

Best,
Samira Patel
Head of Procurement | Acme Systems
Attachment: Acme-RFP-brief.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme onramp & ops handoff proposal

Samira — thanks for the clarity. Quick answers up front, then proposed next steps:

- Pricing: we can match the competitor's effective year-one economics via a staged credit structure (not a permanent list-price change). Proposed structure: 25% onboarding credit applied over the first 3 billing cycles + an operational credit for any missed latency SLOs during month 1-3. Detailed breakdown in ACME-pricing-workbook.xlsx.
- Audit logs: yes — 13-month retention with API export. We will include a short audit export runbook in the SOW.
- SLA: we are willing to add a performance credit clause for sustained misses beyond threshold. We typically structure it as service credits capped at X% of monthly invoice; if you need a higher cap we can route to legal for exception.

Connor, can you confirm the 90-day ops handoff checklist and the runbook items we referenced on the call? We want to avoid transfer friction and make the production cutover predictable.

If these terms look directionally OK, I can prepare an updated PDF and a DocuSign-ready SOW. Would you like the pricing in a single PO-friendly line or broken into pilot + production phases?

Attachment: ACME-pricing-workbook.xlsx

—Jordan

Subject: Fwd: Acme onramp & ops handoff proposal — need pricing OK

Neha — looping you in for pricing/finance sign-off. Acme pushed back that a competitor is offering ~30% effective discount for year one via credits. I proposed a 25% staged onboarding credit + operational SLO credits. See the pricing workbook attached.

Key ask: can we approve 25% onboarding credit applied across the first three invoices for this deal and allow a capped performance credit clause (recommended cap: 10% monthly)? If not, what alternative structures would keep us competitive while protecting unit economics?

Why I want this: Acme is a strategic target in healthcare vertical and the deal size is forecasted at $1.2M ARR if production takes. Losing to price here likely blocks additional expansion in their segmentation.

Attachment: ACME-pricing-workbook.xlsx

Thanks — Jordan

On Tue, 29 Jun 2027 at 08:23 Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jordan —

> > - Production commit: 12-month minimum at tiered pricing (we keep list price but apply a one-time onboarding credit in billing)
> > - Performance credit: limited to 10% of the affected month, capped at two months per rolling 12 months

Confirming I have approved the conditional 25% onboarding credit with the packaging constraints below:

- 25% onboarding credit amortized across first two invoices (15% pilot invoice, 10% first production invoice)

Samira —

Appreciate the speed here. Per our internal review we are comfortable with the following final commercial terms:

- Pilot + migration: 25% onboarding credit (15% applied to pilot invoice, 10% applied to first production invoice)
- Production commitment: 12-month minimum to realize full credit
- Performance credit: up to 10% of a monthly invoice, capped at two months in any rolling 12 months
- Audit logs: 13 months retention with API export (included)

We updated the offer and SOW; DocuSign is live here: https://www.docusign.com/sign/xyz-ACME-4892. HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/ACME-2027-PO-4892.
